title: promote-release: refuse a --version older than the current latest, or not plain X.Y.Z, before any move (twin of lore-cli LCLI-631)
description:
Quest's twin of lore-cli LCLI-631. lore-cli relayed it on 2026-09-28 as orchestrator ruling A, arising from the QCLI-391 / LCLI-617 prior-latest pairing: planPromotion refuses a --version strictly older than the current latest, before any move. The refusal message names both versions and says backports are not a promote use case.

PROVENANCE: this was received as a RELAY through lore-cli, not read from an opum-doc record. Before implementing, read the ruling where it is recorded: opum-doc docs/adr/, or opum-agent's tracker. If there is no record, ask opum-agent. Do not build on the relay.

Quest's equivalent is the pre-move planning in scripts/promote-release.mjs, the --promote/dry-run path that plans which dist-tags move. QCLI-391 (#353) covers the rollback record's prior-latest ordering. This is the forward direction: promoting an older version onto latest.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The ruling is read from opum-doc docs/adr/refuse-a-lore-quest-promotion-that-would-move-npm-latest-backwards.md, including its Amendment 1 (read at opum-doc 3142e69), and cited on this task before implementation

promote-release.mjs refuses, on dry run and --promote and before any dist-tag moves, when --version is strictly older than the current npm latest; the message names both versions and says backports are not a promote use case

A fresh promote also refuses, before any write, a --version that is not plain X.Y.Z (e.g. 1.0.0-beta.1); the message says a prerelease, like a backport, belongs on a non-latest dist-tag via a separate path not yet built. Per the amendment, both cases are enforced by validating plan.record with {version} before the first write, not by a second parallel check
Equal and newer plain versions are unaffected; each refusal (older, prerelease) is covered by a test that fails against the pre-change script
lore-cli confirms the refuse/accept verdicts match LCLI-631 (including its AC5 prerelease clause) at both final heads

implementationNotes: SCOPE ADDED 2026-09-28: the prerelease clause, twinning LCLI-631 AC5. lore-cli relayed it, and I verified it against the record rather than the relay. opum-doc docs/adr/refuse-a-lore-quest-promotion-that-would-move-npm-latest-backwards.md, read at opum-doc 3142e69 (dev == main at the time), carries "Amendment 1 — 2026-09-28: also refuse a prerelease --version at the same gate". A fresh promote refuses any --version that is not plain X.Y.Z before any write. A prerelease, like a backport, belongs on a non-latest dist-tag via a separate path not yet built. The mechanism is to validate plan.record with {version} before the first write, which covers the older and the prerelease cases together. The acceptance criteria were rewritten to add this (new AC3). All the originals were unchecked, so no state was lost. AC1 now names the ADR as the recorded source, so the provenance caveat in the description is resolved.

2026-09-28, implemented on branch feat/QCLI-402-refuse-backwards-promotion.

RULING READ (AC1): opum-doc docs/adr/refuse-a-lore-quest-promotion-that-would-move-npm-latest-backwards.md, read at opum-doc main 3142e69 through the gh API, including "Amendment 1 — 2026-09-28: also refuse a prerelease --version at the same gate". The mechanism the amendment names is to validate plan.record with {version} before the first write.

WHAT: planPromotion (scripts/promote-release.mjs) runs on the dry run and on --promote, before main() writes the record or moves a tag. On a fresh run, and not on a resume, it now calls validateRecord(record, {version, packages}) on the record it would return. If that fails, it refuses. The refusal leads with a headline that explains it. When a package's prior latest is newer than the version, the headline names the package and both versions and says backports are not a promote use case. When the version is not plain X.Y.Z, the headline says a prerelease, like a backport, belongs on a non-latest dist-tag through a separate path that is not built. The headlines only explain a refusal and never refuse on their own. A test asserts that the plan's verdict equals validateRecord's verdict on 25 inputs. A resumed run keeps the first record, which main() already validates. Quest has no --version flag: the version is package.json's, so a prerelease reaches this gate only if package.json carries one.

EVIDENCE:
- test/qcli402-refuse-backwards-promotion.test.ts has 6 tests. Against the pre-change script, the 4 refusal tests FAILED (older, one package newer, prerelease or build metadata, and the verdict-equals-validateRecord grid). The 2 unaffected-case guards passed (newer in numeric order past 2^53, and equal refused fresh but accepted on resume).
- Mutation M1 disabled the validateRecord call: exactly the predicted 4 went red. Mutation M2 dropped the headlines: exactly the predicted 3 message tests went red, and the verdict grid stayed green.
- bun run check: 884 pass, 0 fail, exit 0. lore check: 0. check:breaking-bump: 0.

OPEN: AC5 is lore-cli's by-ref verdict match against LCLI-631 at both final heads. LCLI-631 is still To Do on lore-cli dev (read 2026-09-28), so quest's shape comes first here.
